html:
Gabon is a small country on the equator on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa, mostly covered by rainforest. The map shows it from 1880, as a French colony and then an independent state.

Its first known inhabitants were forest hunter-gatherers; Bantu-speaking farmers settled later, and the Fang moved in from the north in the 1800s.

France made a treaty with a local king in 1839 and in 1849 settled people freed from a captured slave ship at a place it named Libreville, "free town". From there Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza explored inland in the 1870s. Gabon became part of French Equatorial Africa, where concession companies cut timber, especially okoumé, with forced labour. In 1913 the doctor Albert Schweitzer opened his hospital at Lambaréné.

Gabon became independent in 1960, in the Year of Africa. Omar Bongo ruled from 1967 until his death in 2009, one of the longest reigns of any African leader, keeping very close ties with France. Oil, manganese and timber made Gabon richer per person than most African countries. His son Ali Bongo succeeded him and was removed by the army in 2023.
sum: Gabon is a small country on the equator on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa, mostly covered by rainforest. The map shows it from 1880, as a French colony and then an independent state.
